items.claim: The verse-initial divine frame that drives this boundary is byte-exact, but the row's corroborating inference that the divine title's recurrence distinguishes this oracle from the siege material before it is contradicted by the bytes, and the mandated rival is grounded on a speech frame that stands nowhere in the material it invokes.
items.evidence: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת stands verse-initially in oshb:Isa.22.15 at byte tier and belongs to the divine-frame class of the messenger formula (the human-speaker frames of that formula sit in the narrative zone, not here), so the onset itself is sound, and the petuchah disclosed at oshb:Isa.22.14 checks out against the parashah inventory at its MT key (tier-3, single witness, correctly declared a non-driver). What fails is the corroboration: the identical title stack אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת closes oshb:Isa.22.14 as a postpositive signature, אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת stands at oshb:Isa.22.12, and a prefixed form stands at oshb:Isa.22.5 (sweep: 8 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, 4 of them in this chapter, at 22:5, 22:12, 22:14 and 22:15) - three of the four inside the very material the row says the title distinguishes it from. What actually distinguishes the unit is the frame's ROLE, verse-initial onset against postpositive signature, which the row never states. Second, the rival sentence grounds the merge on a messenger formula shared with the installation material, but no such formula stands anywhere in oshb:Isa.22.20-Isa.22.24 (that census carries exactly one verse in this chapter, 22:15); the byte-true ground for the rival is the second-person-masculine-singular address chain כֻּתָּנְתֶּ֗ךָ / וְאַבְנֵֽטְךָ֙ / וּמֶֽמְשֶׁלְתְּךָ֖ at oshb:Isa.22.21, which resumes the address of 22:16-19 across this row's own closing seam and is rendered as address by both witnesses - “and I will clothe him with your robe, and strengthen him with your belt. I will commit your government into his hand” (web:Isa.22.21).

items.claim: The row's only declared substrate signal, a fresh addressee shift at its opening verse, is contradicted by the bytes: the addressee does not change there, and the second-person address of the officer sentenced at 22:15-19 continues inside this row's own span, undisclosed.
items.evidence: oshb:Isa.22.20 does open on a day-formula scene onset, וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא (byte tier; sweep: 45 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, 4 of them in this chapter, at 22:8, 22:12, 22:20 and 22:25), and that onset would carry the seam. But the newly named steward enters as a third-person OBJECT of the divine verb, לְעַבְדִּ֔י לְאֶלְיָקִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.22.20, byte tier), while the grammatical ADDRESSEE one verse later is still the officer addressed from 22:16 on: כֻּתָּנְתֶּ֗ךָ, וְאַבְנֵֽטְךָ֙ and וּמֶֽמְשֶׁלְתְּךָ֖ at oshb:Isa.22.21 are all second-person-masculine-singular suffix forms, and both witnesses render them as address - “and I will clothe him with your robe, and strengthen him with your belt. I will commit your government into his hand” (web:Isa.22.21). The seam is therefore a referent and scene shift, not an addressee shift; that address chain straddles the row's own opening seam and argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed, while the rival sentence disputes only the far seam and asserts there that the addressee is unchanged - the opposite of what the opening claim requires. Correcting the driver re-opens this row's substrate-signal list, which carries this single contested key and no other. The remaining byte work is clean: the inventories return 0 parashah marks, 0 ketiv/qere notes and 0 special-letter segs inside 22:20-24, the 1 seg site in the span is disclosed count-only with no position claimed, and the named-steward servant class is correctly kept apart from the book's unnamed servant-figure zones with no referent decided.

items.claim: The row's deliberate-recurrence disclosure is byte-false: the postpositive divine signature it pairs with the day formula stands at exactly one verse in the whole header-bounded oracle, so the pairing it says is repeated has no second site.
items.evidence: נְאֻם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.22.25, byte tier) is the sole postpositive-signature token in the header-bounded valley-of-vision oracle: a finals-normalized exact-token sweep of that signature returns 23 verses book-wide and exactly 1 in this chapter (22:25). The earlier scene-shift sub-unit the row invokes opens on the day formula ALONE - וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא (oshb:Isa.22.20, byte tier) - with no signature token anywhere in 22:20-24. The day formula itself does recur in the oracle (sweep: 4 verses in this chapter, at 22:8, 22:12, 22:20 and 22:25), but the claimed signature-plus-formula PAIRING occurs once, and the disclosure carries no tier label for a recurrence it asserts as deliberate. Everything else in the row holds and the chapter's own trap is handled correctly: the closing הַמַּשָּׂ֣א אֲשֶׁר עָלֶ֔יהָ (oshb:Isa.22.25, byte tier) is read as the common burden noun and kept apart from the verse-initial header class that opens this chapter and the next, and the setumah at that verse checks out against the parashah inventory (tier-3, single witness, non-driver), though it is cited under a translation-side prefix rather than the MT key that inventory uses, and the English gloss offered alongside the closing splice covers a verb the spliced Hebrew run does not include.

items.claim: The inclusio driver is true at the tier the row honestly names, but the bracket is built without disclosing that the same imperative cry also stands mid-span, and the row's declared speech-frame key asserts a divine-name adjacency the cited verse's bytes do not carry.
items.evidence: Verified as stated: הֵילִ֣ילוּ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֗ישׁ (oshb:Isa.23.1) and הֵילִ֖ילוּ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֑ישׁ (oshb:Isa.23.14) are NOT byte-identical but ARE identical once cantillation is removed, consonants and vowel points agreeing, and the three-token cry returns exactly 2 verses book-wide at that tier - the tier label is honest and the pair is real. The undisclosed fact is that the imperative itself also stands inside the span at oshb:Isa.23.6, הֵילִ֖ילוּ יֹ֥שְׁבֵי אִֽי (byte tier; exact-token sweep: 4 verses book-wide, 3 of them inside this row's own span, at 23:1, 23:6 and 23:14). A cry that recurs mid-span weakens its own recurrence at the span's end as a closing bracket, and the row offers no occurrence digit for the object it brackets with. Second, the row's declared speech-frame key asserts divine-name adjacency at oshb:Isa.23.12, but וַיֹּ֕אמֶר there carries no divine name in its own bytes and that adjacency census returns 0 verses in this chapter; the speaker is carried over from יְהוָה֙ צִוָּ֣ה at oshb:Isa.23.11 (byte tier), a defensible in-span inference but not the census object the key names. Third, the word-bound proper-name claim is byte-TRUE - the city name צֹ֑ר (oshb:Isa.23.1, byte tier) stands 3 times in 3 verses inside the span, at 23:1, 23:5 and 23:8, every one of them the two-consonant spelling, with no rock-epithet form and no adversary form present - but the digit cited for it reports the span's length rather than the swept object's count. Disclosure is otherwise complete and correct: both ketiv/qere notes in the span are disclosed at their bearing verses with apparatus pairs that re-collate at byte tier, both seg sites are cited count-only and position-free, and the setumah at the span's close checks out at its MT key.

items.claim: The scene-shift onset, the closing seam and the entire disclosure layer of this row are byte-verified and complete, with the day formula standing verse-initially at the row's opening and nowhere else in the chapter.
items.evidence: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וְנִשְׁכַּ֤חַת צֹר֙ stands verse-initially at oshb:Isa.23.15 at byte tier and is the only day-formula onset in this chapter (sweep: 45 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, 1 in this chapter), a tier-1 seam under the frame policy and a stronger signal than the rival merge the row discloses. קֹ֚דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָ֔ה re-collates at byte tier in oshb:Isa.23.18. Every disclosure object in and adjacent to the span checks out against the inventories at MT keys and is correctly typed: setumah immediately before the span at MT 23:14, one seg site inside it at MT 23:17 cited count-only with no position claimed, petuchah at MT 23:18 - the two parashah types are never conflated and both are declared non-drivers; the inventories return 0 ketiv/qere notes and 0 special-letter segs in 23:15-18, and the row claims neither. The row also holds the historical referent of the seventy years open rather than deciding it, which the bytes support: no king is named there.

items.claim: The row's undigited universal denial of any divine-speech frame inside its span is contested by the divine-utterance authentication formula standing at its third verse, the very formula cited at 22:25 in this same range as an oracle-closing signature, and that same verse is the row's one undisclosed seg site.
items.evidence: כִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה דִּבֶּ֖ר אֶת הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה stands at oshb:Isa.24.3 (byte tier); its twin כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר closes oshb:Isa.22.25 (byte tier), where the same formula is cited as part of that oracle's closing signature (skeleton-tier sweep of the formula: 10 verses book-wide, 2 of them inside this cluster's range, at 22:25 and 24:3). Either the formula is a divine-speech signal, in which case the row's statement that no divine-speech frame appears anywhere in this row is false and 24:3 is an undisclosed in-span signal carrying a rival closing function at 24:3|24:4 that the row never weighs, or it is not, in which case its use as closing evidence at 22:25 is overstated; the same range cannot hold both, and the denial carries no sweep digit either way. The row's other two denials do check out against the named censuses, which return 0 oracle-header verses and 0 woe-onset verses in this chapter, and the remnant claim is exact and correctly class-split: the verb-family members stand at oshb:Isa.24.6 and oshb:Isa.24.12 and at no other verse in the span (sweep: 2 verses in span), held apart from the noun, the collective noun and the personal name that share the root; but it is made with an unpointed form alone while being listed as a substrate signal, so it does not reach the pointed-splice bar that listing implies. Finally the one in-span seg object, 2 segs at MT 24:3, count-only and single-witness, is undisclosed although the row engages the mark layer and the same object is disclosed at 22:24, 23:1, 23:13 and 23:17 elsewhere in this range. The parashah statement itself is true: the inventory returns 0 petuchah and 0 setumah marks inside 24:1-13, and the petuchah closing the preceding unit at MT 23:18 is correctly keyed and typed.

items.claim: The row opens on a bare third-person-plural pronoun whose antecedent lies outside its span, leaving an anaphoric dependency straddling its own opening seam undisclosed, and a supporting statement about the enumerated sung-praise sites is inaccurate as written.
items.evidence: oshb:Isa.24.14 opens הֵ֛מָּה יִשְׂא֥וּ קוֹלָ֖ם (byte tier), an independent third-person-plural pronoun with no antecedent anywhere inside 24:14-15; the referent is supplied by the gleaning image that ends the preceding verse, כְּנֹ֣קֶף זַ֔יִת (oshb:Isa.24.13, byte tier), which sits outside this row's span. Both witnesses read the pronoun as resumptive - “These shall lift up their voice.” (web:Isa.24.14) - so the dependency is byte-true and argues continuity across this row's own opening seam, yet the rival sentence disputes only the far seam at 24:16 and the opening seam is left unargued. The imperative form-class claim does hold: כַּבְּד֣וּ יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.24.15, byte tier) is read as a plural imperative by both witnesses, and the setumah at that verse checks out against the parashah inventory as a tier-3 single-witness non-driver, though it too is cited under a translation-side prefix rather than the MT key. Two smaller items: the divine-title key names the bare tetragrammaton, which is present twice in the span, but the same verse also carries a compound title stack that is a different count-object and goes unnamed; and the prose states that the enumerated sung-praise sites begin at Isa.25.1, which is false book-wide, since a sung-praise unit is enumerated at chapter 12 far earlier, besides putting campaign apparatus into row prose where the register bars it.

items.claim: The row's closing seam rests on a tier-3 single-witness mark alone: the tier-1 day-formula onset standing at the very next verse, the same onset treated as a driver at 22:20, 22:25 and 23:15, is neither quoted nor referenced, so the close is formally undriven.
items.evidence: The opening work is sound and the hardest trap in the span is handled: א֣וֹי לִ֑י (oshb:Isa.24.16, byte tier) is correctly identified as the distinct exclamation lexeme and never blended with the woe-series onset word, בֹּגְדִ֣ים בָּגָ֔דוּ (oshb:Isa.24.16, byte tier) is quoted for the threading argument into the terror imagery, the mid-verse turn from reported song to personal cry is held open rather than decided, and the layout fold at that verse is correctly marked as layout and denied evidentiary weight. The failure is at the other end. The row's stated ground for stopping at 24:20 is a setumah at that verse, an object campaign policy bars from driving a boundary, while oshb:Isa.24.21 opens וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (byte tier), the identical day-formula onset treated as a tier-1 driver at 22:20, 22:25 and 23:15 in this same range, and the sole site of that formula in this chapter (sweep: 45 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, 1 in this chapter). Neither the formula nor the verse carrying it appears in the row's prose or in its evidence refs, and the prose describes 24:17-20 as sustained imagery without saying why the sequence stops. Disclosure inside the span is otherwise complete and correctly typed: setumah at MT 24:20 inside the span and at MT 24:15 immediately before it, and the inventories return 0 seg sites, 0 ketiv/qere notes and 0 special-letter segs in 24:16-20, none of which the row claims.
